newsitem.title: CHINA: China says fights 'snake head' people smugglers.
newsitem.headline: China says fights 'snake head' people smugglers.

text.p: China is cracking down on criminal gangs that smuggle people abroad from the southeastern province of Fujian, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.
So-called "snakeheads" behind the illegal trade had cheated would-be emigrants out of their money and created immigration problems in the United States and other countries, Xinhua said.
The central government and local officials were trying to curb the problem, the news agency quoted You Dexin, a Fujian provincial government adviser as saying.
"Cracking down on illegal emigration has been an important part of government work in Changle and Lianjiang counties, where illegal emigration was most serious," he said.
Gangs in China and abroad had formed a global smuggling network, You said, without giving details of measures used to curb the trade.
Many Chinese from coastal areas such as Fujian pay fees as high as $30,000 each to leave China in search of more prosperous lives in the United States or Japan.
Once at their destinations, they are often forced to work as indentured servants or in brothels, or are held prisoner by the smugglers for ransoms from their families back in China.
In December, Japanese authorities seized a fishing vessel with 100 suspected Chinese illegal immigrants aboard.
In 1993 a decrepit cargo ship ran aground off New York City, carrying 286 Chinese hoping to start new lives in the United States. Ten of the passengers drowned.
